**Candidate solutions:** Prepare from the existing fork branch when reusing a PR, or record the expected remote branch OID and push the agent-owned install branch with `--force-with-lease`. Add a real git regression test for rerunning against an existing fork branch with prior commits.

**Comments:** Codex marked this blocking. Claude and the rubrics review did not raise it, but the current code supports the failure mode.

Short answer: no, this CLI is not an `implement`-like agent route by itself.

What PR #285 adds is a deterministic fork/PR helper:

- `prepare`: validates `owner/repo`, requires `GH_TOKEN` from `AGENT_INSTALL_PAT`, confirms the target is public, checks existing install PRs, creates/reuses the token owner’s fork, clones the target, and checks out `agent/install-agent-infra`. See `.agent/src/install-fork-pr.ts` around [`prepareInstallForkPr`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/c5ca80af6e4274092611edabee6673117863e8dc/.agent/src/install-fork-pr.ts#L448-L459).
- then the **install skill/agent** does the actual investigation/copy/audit/test/commit work in that returned checkout. See the skill flow at [`.skills/install-agent/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/c5ca80af6e4274092611edabee6673117863e8dc/.skills/install-agent/SKILL.md#L113-L211).
- `publish`: pushes the current checkout `HEAD` to the fork branch, then reuses or opens a PR against the original target repo. See [`publishInstallForkPr`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/c5ca80af6e4274092611edabee6673117863e8dc/.agent/src/install-fork-pr.ts#L510-L599).

So the overall `/install owner/repo` flow is:

```text
route auth + AGENT_INSTALL_PAT
-> helper prepare fork/worktree
-> install-agent skill investigates target and installs files
-> helper publish fork branch / target PR
```

The helper itself does **not** spin up a separate `/implement` route. It is just the safe GitHub mechanics used by the install skill.

On CLI style: agreed. Current PR uses env-heavy examples like:

```sh
GH_TOKEN="$GH_TOKEN" INSTALL_TARGET_REPO="<owner/repo>" node .agent/dist/cli/install-fork-pr.js prepare
```

The cleaner interface would be closer to:

```sh
GH_TOKEN="$GH_TOKEN" node .agent/dist/cli/install-fork-pr.js prepare --target-repo <owner/repo>
GH_TOKEN="$GH_TOKEN" node .agent/dist/cli/install-fork-pr.js publish --target-repo <owner/repo> --workdir <path> --fork-repo <owner/repo> --default-branch <branch> --branch <branch> --pr-title <title> --pr-body-file <path>
```

I’d keep `GH_TOKEN` as env, not `--github-token <value>`, so the token does not show up in process args/logs.
